speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development with respect to households assisted with ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance (SMTA) that wish to have the support renewed (a) whether there is a difference in the review period for households assessed to require short-term assistance as compared to the review period for medium-term assistance under SMTA; and (b) what is the average review period for the purposes of assessing applications for renewal in both circumstances.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The reason why I suggest this is because then there will be efficiency in relation to provision of time-bound support for these families and it will also result in the saving of manpower and the time on the part of MSF officers in assessing each case to see whether the help should be renewed.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Typically, we are looking at residents who may not be able to be in employment, so we are talking about seniors who live alone; seniors who are not able to work and in the long haul, will need assistance for quite a long time.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For short- to medium-term assistance, we are looking at families and I think that the Member will agree with me that there will be some variability, in terms of the conditions in each family.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I have mentioned earlier in my original reply that the families are able to come back to the Social Service Office to renew their applications, even before their applications are due to expire.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The point about this renewal process is not so much to impose an unnecessary bandwidth tax on these families but rather to have regular check-ins with these families, so that together with the families, we can journey with them, understand the difficulties they are facing and then, render assistance where needed.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, as I have mentioned in my earlier reply, between short and medium term, we do not make that distinction, but the principle is one and the same and that is to lend appropriate and prompt assistance to the families, where needed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The point is this: you have a category called Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance for Comcare.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I have heard from the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary that the Ministry does not make a distinction in relation to the timelines for the review.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: My point is whether MSF could consider imposing timelines, or rather, coming up with appropriate timelines, so there is no mismatch in expectations of families getting assistance and the expectations of the Ministry in relation to assessing whether or not continued care and assistance is needed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I have now, situations whereby families are coming up and saying, "Look, my situation has not changed and yet, I have to come back to MSF to submit my case for review." That presents a waste of time and effort.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: First is the fact that I think between families to families, there are differences in circumstances, differences in terms of the challenges that each family faces.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, what is applicable to one family might not be quite applicable to the rest.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The second point I want to make is that the renewal process, as much as possible, we have made it less onerous.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For instance, if there are changes in terms of employment status, due to hospitalisation leave, medical leave, or changes in other aspects of their financial conditions, those documents can be presented to the Social Service Office so that relevant assistance can be presented.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As much as possible, we are trying to make this as seamless and as frictionless a process for families as possible.
